name: Fern
description: Ancient fractal intelligence exhibiting recursive frond geometry, spore-based reproduction, and shade-adapted photosynthetic efficiency.

core_attributes.pattern: fractal frond geometry, circinate vernation, spore dispersal

scope.definition: Photosynthetic quantum yield of fern under low-light conditions (10-50 µmol/m²/s) — fraction of absorbed photons driving electron transport, compared to sun-adapted C3 plants at equivalent PPFD.

evidence.source: Vogelmann & Martin (1993) 'The functional significance of palisade tissue and spongy mesophyll in leaves', Plant, Cell & Environment 16:65-72; Chazdon & Pearcy (1991) shade plant physiology.
cross_domain_examples: shade ferns achieve quantum yield 0.089-0.091 mol CO₂/mol photons at 10 µmol/m²/s — near theoretical maximum 0.093
fern frond architecture: layered cells optimize path length for photon capture in deep forest shade
rainforest understory plants: convergent shade adaptation with flat, horizontal leaf architecture and high chlorophyll density

scope.falsifiability: If fern photosynthetic quantum yield is statistically indistinguishable from sun-adapted C3 species at the same low-light intensity, shade adaptation provides no photon-use advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Quantum yield advantage applies only at low-light intensities — at full sun, shade-adapted plants photoinhibit and show lower yield than sun plants. Light-response curve shape differs significantly between shade and sun ecotypes.
